analysis.title: Signal over Noise: Shifting gears for the year ahead – Bonds in the lead, equities to Neutral
key_insights: UBS CIO sees an inflection point with the highest yields in over 20 years and the highest disruption risk to megacap tech. Advice is to lock in medium-term bond yields and use equity rallies to diversify from concentrated index holdings.
Framework uses three lenses: macro data, company fundamentals, and structural trends. The headline call is bonds in the lead and equities moved to Neutral.
Macro lens: the US GDP impulse from government spending steps down from 0.4% to 0.1% next year, while inflation stays near 4% on sticky services and slowing shelter disinflation.
Household and government safety margins are thinner. Savings rate has fallen to 3.8% from 6% a year ago, and benchmark rates remain almost a full percentage point higher.

Fundamentals lens: S&P 500 trades around 18x forward earnings after a 17% upward revision to profit estimates over the past year, the largest since 2020-2021. UBS sees limited room for upside beyond its 15% earnings growth forecast for next year.
AI lens: aggregate free cash flow of the five largest hyperscalers is set to turn negative next year, forcing reliance on debt and external financing for data center expansion.

AI agents now account for over 75% of total AI token usage, up from under 5% a year ago. A shift from B2C to B2A (business-to-agents) threatens advertising and SaaS, the largest and most profitable tech markets.
A record wave of large-cap private companies entering public markets rivals the largest public firms in scale and competes for portfolio space and economic profits.
Portfolio actions: reduce concentration risk, with equal-weighted strategies already outperforming broad benchmarks this year and expected to keep doing so.
Lock in fixed income yields, with the 10-year Treasury around 5%, to secure income and position for price gains when rates eventually fall.

Negative hyperscaler FCF, agent-driven B2A shift, and large IPO supply create disruption risk.
